subject: Removing individual missing nearly all marker data

messages.author: f5cb6d626f60e415
messages.subject: Removing individual missing nearly all marker data
parts: I am trying to remove a specific individual, "CD174_1" , who is missing a lot of marker data. My csv is rotated, I have a "ID" row with the names of the individuals. I tried to use the subset function but it gave me an error. I can start the process over removing that from my CSV but I would prefer to just learn this subset function better.  Thank you!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Removing individual missing nearly all marker data
parts:
Could you show the code you used, and the error?

One way to drop the individuals with the most missing data is using nmissing() to count the number of missing genotypes for each individual. Here's an example.

library(qtl)
data(hyper)
nmis <- nmissing(hyper)
hypersub <- subset(hyper, ind= (nmis < max(nmis)) )

nind(hyper) # 250
nind(hypersub) # 240  (10 individuals missing exactly 133 markers)

karl

messages.subject: Re: Removing individual missing nearly all marker data
parts:
match() in this case is going to return a single value, and then is.na(match( ) ) is going to be either TRUE or FALSE, according to whether "CD174_1" is found within mycross$pheno$id.
The ind argument in the subset.cross() function needs either a numeric index or a vector of TRUE/FALSE with length being the number of individuals.

I think this might work:

mycross <- subset(mycross, ind= -match(ind2drop, mycross$pheno$id))

That is, use match() to get the numeric index and then make it negative to take all the others but not this one.

karl
